brief.outcome: Grow active members from 610 to 750 by June 1 by closing the gap between about 40 joins and about 45 cancellations a month, while keeping the no lock-in promise.

ambition.goal_beyond: A gym that grows because members stay and say why they leave, so growth does not depend on ad spend alone
rungs: Bring in more joins with a Meta campaign inside the $2,000 monthly budget
Find out who cancels, when, and why (members have never been asked), and fix the biggest cause of cancellations as well as joins
Keep it true: a monthly check of joins, cancellations by join-month group and early attendance that flags a slide before it costs a quarter
ambition.judge: The Mindbody report of active members, joins and cancellations by month and by join-month group, read against the 610 baseline and the 750 target

brief.deliverable: A checked picture of who cancels and when, a first set of reasons from members themselves, a retention and onboarding routine that keeps no lock-in, a compliant Meta campaign launched with the owners' approval inside budget, and a monthly readout of active members against 750
done: Member counts rebuilt from Mindbody exports and reconciled month by month
Lead and join tracking from Meta to Mindbody checked, or its limits stated
Diagnosis with every hypothesis marked supported, refuted or unknown
Partners' choice recorded, with reasons where the top option is passed over
Survey wording, onboarding messages and ads built and checked against the no lock-in promise and Meta ad rules
Ads created paused, read back and switched on only with approval; any message to members approved first
Monthly readout of active members against 750 with guardrails checked
guardrails: Members can still cancel in one step, with no contract, fee or lock-in
Marketing spend stays at or below $2,000 in any month
Cost per new member stays below what a member is worth to the gym, once the owners set that figure
Monthly cancellations do not rise above about 45 while joins grow
All ad copy and images follow Meta health and wellness ad rules
limits: No long-term contracts and no lock-in tactics
Mindbody data comes by export only
Working data lives in a Google Sheet
Anything sent to members or posted live is approved first
assets: Meta Ads account reachable through the Meta Ads MCP
brief.data_home: A Google Sheet, as the owners asked; member IDs only, names and contact details stay in Mindbody
brief.technical_level: Not stated; ready drafts and plain steps, with the owners sending anything to members
brief.decides: The owner and the partner together
unknowns: What a member is worth (price, margin and typical stay)
Where the 40 new joins a month come from today
Whether class capacity limits growth at peak times
How fast and how well new leads and trials are followed up
How Mindbody counts frozen or paused members in the 610 active

answers.question: The business
answers.answer: Independent gym in Denver with group classes

answers.question: Where are members now and what moves
answers.answer: 610 active members, about 45 cancellations and 40 new joins a month (Mindbody report)

answers.question: Tools and access
answers.answer: Instagram 3,100 followers; Meta Ads MCP connected with live access; Mindbody exports only

answers.question: Brand promise
answers.answer: No long-term contracts; known for no lock-in and want to keep that

research.approach: Practitioners treat a membership number as a leaky bucket: net growth equals joins minus cancellations, and with about 45 leaving against 40 joining the gym shrinks by about 5 a month. They rebuild the member count from the raw Mindbody exports, split cancellations by how long the member stayed and how often they came, and ask leavers why in a short, honest survey before changing anything. Early attendance is the strongest warning sign, so new-member onboarding in the first six weeks is a standard lever. Paid social comes second, with ads that follow the platform's health and wellness rules and a fast, tracked follow-up on every lead. Changes are compared against a control, such as alternate join weeks, so the season does not get the credit. For a gym known for no lock-in, retention tools must never add cancellation friction.

sources.title: Meta Advertising Standards: Health and wellness
sources.note: Platform policy: weight loss ads must target adults 18 and over and cannot imply inferiority; fitness services and health clubs are treated as general wellbeing ads. Last change dated 23 July 2026.

sources.title: From Occasional to Steady: Habit Formation Insights From a Comprehensive Fitness Study (arXiv 2501.01779)
sources.note: Research: in one large club's data about half of new members had lost their attendance streak by week six; those who stayed had roughly nine visits in six weeks. One club in one country, so test it on our own data. (arXiv id 2501.01779 means January 2025; exact day not confirmed; accessed 2026-11-03)

sources.title: Mindbody: Business reporting and analytics
sources.note: Platform page: reports cover client retention, membership status, attendance, first visits, cancellations; filter by date, staff or service and export as CSV. (no date shown on the page; accessed 2026-11-03)

sources.title: Meta for Developers: Lead ads
sources.note: Platform documentation: lead ads can pass leads to a CRM as they arrive, which makes fast follow-up possible; sharing CRM outcomes back can improve lead quality. (no date shown on the page; accessed 2026-11-03)

steps.name: Rebuild the member count and monthly joins and cancellations from the raw exports
steps.why: 610, 40 and 45 are reports until the member-level export reproduces them, and definitions (frozen, paused) change the answer.

steps.name: Split cancellations by time as a member and by recent attendance
steps.why: A leak in the first weeks needs a different fix from a leak after a year.

steps.name: Check class fill and booking limits at peak and off-peak times
steps.why: Full classes turn away members and leads, and empty ones cost the gym atmosphere.

steps.name: Check where leads and trials come from and how fast they are followed up
steps.why: A campaign only helps if its leads are tracked into Mindbody and contacted quickly.

steps.name: Ask people who left why, with a short survey that is easy to answer
steps.why: Nobody has asked, so every explanation is a guess until members say it.

steps.name: Build a first six weeks routine for new members
steps.why: Early attendance habits predict who stays, so a planned start is the cheapest retention lever.

steps.name: Launch a small, compliant Meta campaign that sends leads to a fast follow-up
steps.why: Joins are the other half of net growth, and health and wellness ads have rules.

steps.name: Read joins, cancellations and early attendance monthly against a control
steps.why: Net growth is the sum of two flows and seasons move both, so changes need a comparison group.

steps.name: Add contracts, notice periods or cancellation fees to hold members
steps.why: A common way to cut cancellations quickly.

pitfalls.text: Reading cancellations without tenure, so an early-weeks leak is hidden inside the average.
Buying joins with ads while the gym loses members at the same rate, so the number never moves.
Treating the 610 as a clean figure when frozen, paused or comped members may be included.
Survey bias: a long form or one sent only to happy members gives reasons that mislead.
Health and wellness ads that imply the viewer's weight or body is a problem are rejected or restricted.
Leads that are not followed up quickly or not matched to Mindbody joins, so ad cost per member cannot be known.

plan.name: Grow active members by keeping them and by joining more

capabilities.name: Google Sheet working data

data.why: Early attendance and the weeks before cancelling, plus class fill.

stages.name: Pin down the goal
stages.goal: Turn the request into a measured goal, a gap in joins and cancellations, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Rebuild the member numbers
stages.goal: Load member, visit, lead and ad data into the Google Sheet and rebuild active members, joins and cancellations by month from the member list.

checks.name: Opening members plus joins minus cancellations equals closing members for each of the last 12 months, and the latest month matches the reported 610 within 5 members, or the gap is explained
How frozen, paused and comped members are counted is stated
The sheet holds member IDs only, no names, emails or phone numbers
Missing fields are named with what each blocks

stages.name: Check leads can be traced to members
stages.goal: Check that Meta leads and trials reach Mindbody with a source, that each lead is counted once, and how fast the front desk replies.

checks.name: Share of joins in the last 3 months that carry a lead source is stated
Meta leads in a sample week match Mindbody prospects within 10%, or the gap is explained
Median time to first reply is stated from the two-week tally
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for cost per member

stages.name: Find who leaves, when and why
stages.goal: Test the hypotheses on tenure, attendance, season, plan, class capacity and lead follow-up, and keep competing explanations. Reasons stay unknown until members answer.

checks.name: Every hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with the numbers used
A finding on a group of fewer than 30 members is marked low-confidence
Each main finding names a competing explanation
States the joins and cancellations per month needed to reach 750 by June 1 (net plus 20 a month on average) and which mix each finding could deliver

stages.name: Rank what to change
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into ranked options (survey, onboarding, at-risk member contact, class changes, Meta campaign) with expected effect on net members, effort, confidence, risk, cost and measurement.

checks.name: Every option cites the finding it rests on
Every option has expected effect on net members, effort, confidence, risk, cost and how it is measured
No option adds a contract, fee, notice period or extra step to cancel
Paid options show a spend limit from the gym's own member value, or say it is unknown and start small

stages.name: Owner and partner choose
stages.goal: Choose the options, the share of the $2,000 for ads, and what is sent to members. Record reasons when the top option is passed over.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over options are in decisions.jsonl
The chosen monthly ad budget is a number at or below $2,000

stages.name: Build the survey and the first six weeks routine
stages.goal: Write a short, easy-to-answer leaver survey, a first six weeks plan for new members with a nudge when early attendance is low, and a contact script for at-risk members. Everything keeps cancelling a single step.

checks.name: The survey has no more than 3 questions, one of them free text, and does not steer answers
No message pressures a member to stay or adds a step to cancel
Each nudge has a clear trigger from the visit data, such as fewer than 2 visits in a week during the first 6 weeks
Messages read as the gym speaking, with a real person to reply to

stages.name: Build the ads and lead follow-up
stages.goal: Draft Meta ad concepts and copy for the chosen offer, using the gym's own class photos and Instagram posts, and a lead follow-up script. Check every ad against Meta health and wellness rules.

checks.name: No ad implies the viewer's weight, body or health is a problem, and none uses before-and-after body images
Every ad and page says there are no contracts, in the gym's own words
Ads differ in angle or audience, not only in wording
The follow-up script sets a first reply within 1 hour in opening hours

stages.name: Send and launch, paused first
stages.goal: Create the Meta campaign paused and read it back; the owners send the survey and switch on onboarding messages. Register the comparison before anything goes live.

checks.name: Campaign, ad sets and ads were created paused and read back from the account
Daily budget times days in the month is at or below $2,000, and the cap is shown on the receipt
The comparison is registered in experiments.jsonl before anything goes live: new members get the new routine by join-week parity (odd weeks new, even weeks as today)
Each message to members was shown to the owners and sent by them

stages.name: Read members each month
stages.goal: Each month read active members, joins, cancellations by join-month group, early attendance, survey answers and cost per new member against the baseline and the control.

checks.name: Active members, joins and cancellations come from the Mindbody export, not from ad or Instagram numbers
The new routine is compared with the alternate-week control on 90-day cancellation, and a verdict needs at least 60 members in each group, otherwise INCONCLUSIVE
Survey results show the number of answers and the share per reason, and reasons from fewer than 20 answers are marked low-confidence
One-step cancelling, the $2,000 cap and cancellations at or below 45 a month are checked

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Close the comparison, record which reasons and routines moved net members, propose rules with their scope and plan the next round.

checks.name: The registered comparison is closed in experiments.jsonl with a verdict
Each proposed rule says whether it holds for this gym or any studio

hypotheses.statement: Most cancellations come from members in their first 90 days.
hypotheses.test: Tenure at cancellation for all cancellations in the last 12 months.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than half of cancellations happen within 90 days of joining.
hypotheses.refute_if: Fewer than a third happen within 90 days.

hypotheses.statement: New members who do not build an early attendance habit leave sooner.
hypotheses.test: Visits in the first 6 weeks against cancelling within 6 months, using the habit threshold of about 9 visits in 6 weeks as the split.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Members under 9 visits in 6 weeks cancel within 6 months at 1.5 times the rate of the rest, with at least 30 members in each group.
hypotheses.refute_if: The two groups cancel at similar rates.

hypotheses.statement: Members who cancel stopped coming weeks before they cancelled.
hypotheses.test: Visits in the 30 days before cancelling against active members of the same tenure.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Cancelling members averaged less than half the visits of active members of the same tenure.
hypotheses.refute_if: Visits were about the same, so cancelling is not preceded by a drop.

hypotheses.statement: Joins and cancellations follow a season, so part of the gap is calendar.
hypotheses.test: Monthly joins and cancellations over 24 months.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The same months are above or below average in both years by 15% or more.
hypotheses.refute_if: No repeat pattern across the two years.

hypotheses.statement: Cancellations cluster in one plan, class type or time slot.
hypotheses.test: Cancellation rate by plan type, main class type and usual visit time.
hypotheses.confirm_if: One group with at least 30 members has a cancellation rate 1.5 times the gym average.
hypotheses.refute_if: Rates are within 20% of the average across groups.

hypotheses.statement: Full peak classes turn members and leads away.
hypotheses.test: Bookings against capacity by class and time, plus late cancels and waitlist use if recorded.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than 30% of peak-time classes are at 90% full or more.
hypotheses.refute_if: Peak classes are rarely above 80% full.

hypotheses.statement: Leads and trials are lost because follow-up is slow or untracked.
hypotheses.test: Median time to first reply, and the share of trials that join, from the lead log.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Median reply is over 1 hour in opening hours, or fewer than 1 in 4 trials joins.
hypotheses.refute_if: Replies are within the hour and trial conversion is healthy.

hypotheses.statement: The $2,000 budget cannot add enough joins at an acceptable cost per member.
hypotheses.test: After 6 weeks: spend divided by joins that carry a Meta lead source, against the gym's own member value.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Cost per new member is above member value, or the budget yields fewer than 10 extra joins a month.
hypotheses.refute_if: Cost per new member is below member value and extra joins are 10 a month or more.

dropped.reason: The owners' brand is no lock-in; contracts, notice periods and cancellation fees are outside their limits.

measurement.window: Monthly. Read the new routine at 90 days per join-week group; read the campaign after at least 6 weeks of spend.
measurement.min_volume: At least 60 new members in each comparison group, and at least 30 members before a group-level finding is called a finding.
measurement.stop_rule: Pause the ads if cost per new member exceeds the gym's own member value for 4 weeks in a row or the monthly cap is reached; stop any message that members report as pressure to stay.
